post.caption: Australia's first gold coin skipped permission. Victoria's gold rush pulled thousands of men out of Adelaide. Diggers returned with gold, but the colony lacked coins to pay them. In January 1852, lawmakers passed the Bullion Act in two hours. The Government Assay Office opened 13 days later. The coins were 22 carat gold, and said so on the back. London had not approved coining gold, so it was technically illegal. London's answer arrived only after the coining was done. Some pounds were later mounted as jewelry. In all, 24,648 were struck, the last on 13 February 1853.
